title: perf(canary): auto-detect latency/throughput regressions and add rollout guards
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: We observed intermittent latency regressions escaping canary rollouts when tail-latency increases but median metrics remain stable. This PR improves the perf-canary pipeline by adding automated detection for throughput regressions and a tiered rollout guard that blocks or throttles rollouts based on multi-quantile latency signals, distribution drift, and throughput drop detection.

What this changes: - Add new detector that evaluates p50/p90/p99 and token throughput deltas with configurable significance thresholds and minimum sample windows. - Introduce a distribution-drift test using the Kolmogorov-Smirnov heuristic on latency samples to catch shape changes. - Add a rollout guard layer that maps detector outputs to actions (allow, slow-rollout, block) and ties into the existing rollout controller. - Harden the canary harness: improved synthetic load generator, deterministic seed for KV cache warmup, and additional integration tests that simulate node-level slowdowns. - Metrics/alerts: new metrics (canary.latency.quantiles, canary.throughput.delta, canary.drift.score) and Grafana dashboard panels + alert rules with sensible defaults. - CI: new perf-smoke workflow that runs the canary harness in CI for fast feedback; CI initially flaked on environment timing and was narrowed to a smaller synthetic load profile.

Compatibility: The rollout guard is additive and disabled by default for existing customers. Config is exposed via canary_policy.yaml with safe defaults.

Testing and validation: - Unit tests for detectors and guard decision logic. - Integration tests that run the harness in a local k8s job (mocked runtime) to validate slow-paths. - Load experiments executed in perf-canary lab: baseline vs patched runtime across 3 model sizes and two HW classes (A100, H100). Results included in internal doc link.

Rollout plan: Feature-flag rollout to internal canaries for 1 week, then opt-in for >= Standard tier customers, monitor canary.throughput.delta and canary.latency.quantiles with a 24h blackout for alerts during rollout ramp.

Checklist:
- [x] Detector implementation
- [x] Rollout guard mapping and config
- [x] Unit and integration tests
- [x] Metrics and dashboard panels
- [x] Documentation and rollout playbook

Notes: See linked Linear items ENG-2148 (auto-detect regressions) and ENG-2199 (rollout guard policy). This addresses recurring post-deploy incidents where model changes caused 10-15% throughput regressions without clear median shifts.

review_comments: Marco Ruiz: Can we reduce the default sample window from 10 minutes to 2 minutes for faster failure detection? Concerned about sensitivity to short-lived spikes.
Aisha Patel: Reduced default window to 3 minutes and made it configurable per-policy. Added a note in docs about trade-offs between sensitivity and false positives.
Sophie Chen: The KS test is O(n log n) — are we safe running it in-line for all canaries? Might need batching or sampling to keep CPU low.
Aisha Patel: Agreed. Added reservoir sampling and a configurable sampling rate; tests show negligible CPU impact in our perf lab runs.
Devon O'Neill: CI perf-smoke flakes on the first run in GitHub Actions; suggest adding a retry and lowering concurrency for GH runner environments.
Aisha Patel: Added a single retry and reduced synthetic load concurrency for CI-only profile. Verified three consecutive runs in CI are green.
release_notes: Add automated detection for latency and throughput regressions and a configurable rollout guard layer to block or throttle canary rollouts when regressions are detected. Disabled by default; configurable via canary_policy.yaml.
